# Charge + Park, The Netherlands (parkingnetherlands.com)

> Every public EV charger and every register-listed parking garage in the Netherlands, priced for a specific stop: charging cost plus parking cost for the time you stay. Independent, free, no sign-up, built on open government data. Published by Analytics Ascent. In English, Dutch, German and French. Last data refresh: 2026-10-05.

## What this site is

A reference and a tool for drivers in the Netherlands. It answers four questions with numbers rather than advice: what a charging stop costs at a given post, what a parking garage charges by the hour and by the day, what street parking costs in each city centre, and what a parking fine is in 2026.

Everything shown is computed from public registers, not copied from operators or municipalities:

- National charge point register (NDW / DOT-NL): 79,147 public charge points, status and tariffs, refreshed every 30 minutes; uptime history kept since 2026-09-28.
- National parking register (NPR / RDW, CC0): 323 garages, car parks and P+R sites in 14 cities, official drive-in tariffs, snapshot 2026-10-04.
- CBS: electric share of private cars per municipality, 1 January 2026.
- Municipal tariff decisions for street parking, and the 2026 Kostenbesluit and CJIB Boetebase for fines.

## Key facts, 2026

- Parking fine for unpaid street parking (naheffingsaanslag): €82.00 cost component plus one hour of the local tariff. Wrong parking under the Mulder regime: €130, €190 with hindrance, €400 to €500 for disabled bays.
- Median public charging price: €0.41 per kWh. Operators range about 15x between cheapest and dearest. 1.6% of charge points are reported out of order at any time.
- Median garage rate across the 14 cities: €2.85 per hour and €62.88 per 24 hours. Cheapest priced garage €0.33 per hour, most expensive €8.00.
- Street parking, city centre, per hour: Amsterdam €8.05, Utrecht €5.10, Rotterdam €4.24, The Hague €3.98, Maastricht €3.60, Haarlem €3.50, Leiden €3.50, Groningen €3.40, Eindhoven €3.30, Nijmegen €3.10, Delft €2.90, Breda €2.80, Tilburg €2.70, Zwolle €2.50.
- Park and Ride: 68 sites, 23,628 spaces, from €2.00 per 24 hours (Groningen, Breda, Tilburg, Zwolle, The Hague) to €6.00 in Amsterdam.
- 16.0% of private cars in the Netherlands are electric, from 28.0% in Rozendaal to 8.2% in Achtkarspelen.
- Public charging power reachable per EV without a driveway: 3.36 kW nationally against the EU benchmark of 1.3 kW, with 8 to 70 neighbourhoods falling short depending on the measure.

## Tools

- https://parkingnetherlands.com/ev-charging : live map of every public charger, priced with parking for your stop. Filters for power (22, 50, 150 kW+), plug (CCS, CHAdeMO), bank card acceptance and faults live in the URL, so a link reproduces a view.
- https://parkingnetherlands.com/search : garages and P+R near any Dutch address, priced for arrival and departure times.
- https://parkingnetherlands.com/map : parking rates in every covered city on one map.
- https://parkingnetherlands.com/street-map : every paid street section in 13 cities coloured by hourly rate.
- https://parkingnetherlands.com/laadpalen : the Dutch charger map, with /laadpaal-<stad> pages for 40 cities and /<exploitant>-storing fault pages per operator (for example /fastned-storing).

## Pages worth citing

- https://parkingnetherlands.com/parking-price-index : garage rates by city, with the full dataset.
- https://parkingnetherlands.com/park-and-ride : all 68 P+R sites with tariffs checked against the municipality.
- https://parkingnetherlands.com/parking-fines : the three fine regimes, 2026 amounts, how to appeal.
- https://parkingnetherlands.com/ev-adoption : EV share per municipality against local charge points.
- https://parkingnetherlands.com/charging-gap : where public charging falls short, per 2 km hexagon.
- https://parkingnetherlands.com/garage/ : directory of all 323 register-listed garages, each with official tariffs, capacity, EV points and height limit. Also /nl/garage/, /de/garage/ and /fr/garage/.
- City guides: /amsterdam, /rotterdam, /the-hague, /utrecht, /eindhoven, /groningen, /maastricht, /leiden, /haarlem, /breda, /delft, /nijmegen, /tilburg, /zwolle, /schiphol and /all-cities. Each city has Dutch (/nl/parkeren-<stad>), German (/de/parken-<stadt>) and French (/fr/stationnement-<ville>) versions.
- Station parking: /parking-amsterdam-centraal, /parking-rotterdam-centraal, /parking-utrecht-centraal, /parking-den-haag-centraal, /parking-eindhoven-station, /parking-groningen-station.
- Guides: /free-parking, /street-parking, /long-term-parking, /parking-apps, /parkbee, /ev-parking, /parking-tips-netherlands.
- https://parkingnetherlands.com/belgium-parking : expat guide to parking in Belgium, with a live free-space map for Ghent.

## Open data published here

- https://parkingnetherlands.com/data/parking-price-index-2026.json and .csv : per-city garage statistics (CC BY 4.0).
- https://parkingnetherlands.com/data/ev-adoption-2026.json and .csv : EV share and charge points per municipality (CC BY 4.0).
- https://parkingnetherlands.com/ev-data/tariffs.json : charging tariffs per operator as used on the map.
- Schema.org Dataset, ParkingFacility, FAQPage and BreadcrumbList markup is on the relevant pages.

## How to cite

Cite as "Parking Netherlands (Analytics Ascent), <page title>, retrieved <date>" with the page URL. Figures are estimates for the stated session; the operator takes the payment and publishes the binding tariff. Every price on the map says which of three sources it comes from: the charger's own tariff, the operator's usual rate, or the national median.

## Crawling

Crawlers that fetch a page to answer a live question and cite the source are welcome everywhere: OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, Claude-SearchBot, Claude-User, PerplexityBot, Perplexity-User, Applebot, Bingbot, DuckDuckBot, YandexBot. See robots.txt for the full policy. Sitemap: https://parkingnetherlands.com/sitemap.xml
